stances.claim: On May 2, 3,992 of 9,183 (43.47%) passed the 2022 Bar and took their oath - restoring the topnotcher announcement (suspended in the combined 2020-2021 cycle when 8,241 of 11,402 / 72.28% passed, 'the highest in history,' partly because no 2020 exam was held due to COVID).
'The ancients in the legal profession, like me' were totally surprised, some even flabbergasted at the gigantic passing percentages - given that the usual average in prior years was about 25%.

'With due respect, I believe the doors to the legal profession should swing on reluctant hinges' - other than the pandemic, no event or reason justifies the doors swinging wide open; CJ does not know that law schools have improved enormously to justify a tsunami of entrants. Having posted his 'Separate Opinion,' he nonetheless yields to and obeys the Court's decision and welcomes the new attorneys.

notable_anecdotes: CJ's 'doors should swing on reluctant hinges' formulation - among his signature single-line articulations of legal-profession entry-gate stewardship, preserved as the operative metaphor of his Separate Opinion register on Bar-passage rates.
The 'ancients in the legal profession, like me' self-identification - a wry generational marker that pairs CJ's institutional standing with humility-as-tribe-name.
The 2020-2021 combined Bar (72.28%) as 'highest in history' - preserved as historical-statistical anchor, with the COVID-no-2020-exam context.
The 'compañeros and compañeras' Spanish-language welcome - CJ's preferred professional-fraternity vocabulary for new lawyers.
CJ's Vision-Mission Statement quoted verbatim from his chief-justiceship - making this column a useful repository of CJ's institutional mission language as carried forward post-retirement.

Joan de Venecia-Fabul's 'wear a badge of incorruptibility' line and the catalog of refusals ('walking away from situations that will require me to sacrifice my dignity and integrity,' 'not taking shortcuts,' 'not arrogantly brandishing the lawyer card to oppress my fellow Filipinos') - one of the most stirring single-Numero-Uno integrity statements preserved in CJ's new-lawyer columns.
Arlene Maneja's Tagalog opener 'Narito na ang exciting part!' - preserving the bilingual register typical of CJ's tribute columns to younger Filipino lawyers.

Maneja's eat-sleep-rest-minimize practical Bar-prep advice - preserved as concrete-care counsel for 2023 examinees, paired with the 'God willing, this would be the only time you'll ever need to take the Bar' closing wish.

Yebra's 'circumstances in which you were born will eventually become immaterial. What you do with your gifts will define who you are' - a particularly clean meritocratic-formation statement from a San Beda graduate now serving as DOTr undersecretary.

one_paragraph_summary: Panganiban welcomes the 3,992 new lawyers who passed the 2022 Bar examinations (43.47% of 9,183) and took their oath before the Supreme Court on May 2 - comparing the 2022 rate with the 2020-2021 combined cycle (no 2020 exam due to COVID; 8,241 of 11,402 / 72.28% passed, 'the highest in history'), and welcoming the 2022 restoration of the topnotcher announcement that the 2020-2021 results had suspended. 'The ancients in the legal profession, like me, were totally surprised, some even flabbergasted at these gigantic passing percentages' given that the usual prior-year average was about 25%. 'With due respect, I believe the doors to the legal profession should swing on reluctant hinges' - other than the pandemic, Panganiban does not know of any event justifying the doors swinging wide open, and is not aware that law schools have improved enormously enough to justify a tsunami of entrants. Having posted his abbreviated 'Separate Opinion,' he nonetheless yields to and obeys the Court's decision and dutifully welcomes the new 'compañeros and compañeras' with his fervent hope and prayer that they fulfill his Vision-Mission Statement (from his chief-justiceship and up to now): 'competent and ethical lawyers who are responsible, dependable, and morally upright; who courageously uphold truth and justice above everything else; and who safeguard the liberty and nurture the prosperity of our people.' He invites three past 'Numero Uno' to greet the new brethren and advise 2023 aspirants. Joan de Venecia-Fabul (2005, UP; first VP and deputy chief legal counsel, PLDT; 2022 Bar examiner for Civil Law II) reflects on 17 years of lawyering, framing the practice as integrity-first - not subverting justice, not 'taking shortcuts,' not 'arrogantly brandishing the lawyer card to oppress my fellow Filipinos' - and exhorts new lawyers to 'choose to do good and act with justice,' 'wear a badge of incorruptibility,' 'seek and speak for the truth,' and help 'when the law is weaponized against those who have less in life.' Arlene M. Maneja (2002, UST; partner, SyCip Salazar Hernandez and Gatmaitan) welcomes new lawyers with 'Narito na ang exciting part!' and the exhortation to be 'fierce warriors for justice and truth' because 'we may not always win but know that there is honor and meaning in fighting the good fight,' offering 2023 aspirants practical Bar-prep advice (be kind; reasonable study plan; eat well, manage sleep, rest; minimize materials; design to do less near exam dates). Reinier R. Yebra (2009, San Beda; undersecretary, Department of Transportation) closes with the meritocratic-formation line: 'the circumstances in which you were born will eventually become immaterial. What you do with your gifts will define who you are.'
